what: Rio Tinto is one of the world's largest mining companies. Iron ore from the Pilbara in Western Australia produces most of its profit, and it also mines copper, aluminium, lithium and minerals.
customers: Chinese and other Asian steelmakers for iron ore, smelters and manufacturers for copper and aluminium.
money: bauxite, alumina and smelting, largely hydro-powered in Canada
Oyu Tolgoi in Mongolia, Escondida stake and Kennecott
moat: Pilbara iron ore deposits with their own railways and ports, among the lowest-cost sources of iron ore in the world.
risks: Iron ore profit depends on Chinese steel demand and construction
Mining projects face long permitting and community consent processes
Oyu Tolgoi in Mongolia carries political and cost risk
Currency moves between the dollar and Australian dollar affect margins
opportunities: Copper production is rising as Oyu Tolgoi's underground mine ramps up
Hydro-powered aluminium sells at a premium to coal-powered metal
A dividend yield near 6% paid from low-cost iron ore cash flow
watch: Pilbara shipment volumes and the copper production ramp at Oyu Tolgoi.
